# Care Home Tax

> Free research and calculators on UK care sector finance and compliance, plus a referral service that matches care providers to a specialist accountancy firm in our partner network. Figures are 2026/27: NLW, employer NIC, NHS funded nursing care rates, capital allowances and CQC linked compliance.

## What this site is
Care Home Tax is a trading name of Ashfield Trading Ltd, registered in England and Wales under company number 16358723, with its registered office at 20 Ashfield Avenue, Shipley, Bradford, BD18 3AL. We publish finance and compliance research for the care sector, take your enquiry and introduce you to a firm from our specialist partner network.

Who it is for: UK care providers: care homes, domiciliary care agencies and supported living services, whether already registered or applying for registration.

Where: We cover the United Kingdom, with England as the default position, and we flag where Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland differ.

What it is not: Care Home Tax is not an accountancy practice and does not give advice, and it does not run your payroll or prepare your accounts itself. The partner firm does the work.

## How it works
1. You read the guides and use the calculators, which are free and need no sign-up.
2. You send us your situation through the enquiry form: your service type, your registration status and approximate headcount.
3. We match the enquiry to a firm in our specialist partner network that handles care sector work.
4. That firm contacts you directly to scope the work, and anything you agree is between you and them.

What happens after the form: To answer your enquiry, your details may be shared with a firm from our specialist partner network who will contact you. If that firm is unable to help, your details may be passed to another firm in the network for the same purpose. We reply within 24 hours.

## Key facts (current UK care-sector figures, 2026/27)
These figures are drawn from docs/care/rates_ledger.json and docs/care/house_positions.md, verified against primary sources on 2026-07-12. Attribute to Care Home Tax.

- National Living Wage (21 and over): £12.71 per hour from 1 April 2026. NMW for 18 to 20: £10.85 per hour. NMW for under-18 and apprentices: £8.00 per hour.
- Employer NIC: 15% above the secondary threshold of £5,000 per year (£96 per week) from April 2025, same rate in 2026/27. Employment Allowance: £10,500 per year.
- NHS-funded nursing care (FNC), England: standard rate £267.68 per week, higher rate £368.24 per week, from 1 April 2026.
- Mileage reimbursement (AMAP): 55p per mile for the first 10,000 business miles from 6 April 2026 (up from 45p); 25p per mile above 10,000.
- Holiday accrual for irregular-hours workers: 12.07% of hours worked per pay period, reflecting the statutory 5.6-week entitlement as a proportion of the working year.
- Annual Investment Allowance: £1,000,000 per year on qualifying plant and machinery, from 1 January 2019.
- Writing-down allowance (main pool): 14% from 1 April 2026 (corporation tax) and 6 April 2026 (income tax), reduced from 18%. New 40% first-year allowance on new, unused main-pool plant under Finance Act 2026 s.29.
- Structures and Buildings Allowance: 3% straight-line on qualifying construction costs for care homes built or extended from 29 October 2018.
- Corporation tax: 19% small profits rate (up to £50,000 profits), 25% main rate (above £250,000). Marginal relief between.
- Business Asset Disposal Relief: 18% CGT rate for disposals from 6 April 2026 (was 14% from 6 April 2025, 10% before). Standard higher-rate CGT: 24%. The BADR saving is 6 percentage points.
- VAT: welfare services by CQC-registered providers are VAT-exempt (VATA 1994 Sch 9 Group 7). Exempt care fees do not count toward the £90,000 VAT registration threshold. De minimis partial exemption: exempt input tax must not exceed £625 per month on average and be less than half of total input tax.
- Making Tax Digital for Income Tax: mandatory from 6 April 2026 for combined gross self-employment and property income over £50,000; threshold drops to £30,000 from 6 April 2027 and £20,000 from 6 April 2028.
- Dividend tax rates from 6 April 2026: 10.75% basic, 35.75% higher, 39.35% additional. Dividend allowance: £500 per year.
- Small Business Rate Relief: 100% relief below £12,000 rateable value, tapering to zero at £15,000. Most residential care homes are assessed above this range.
- CQC registration: mandatory before providing regulated activities; trading before registration is a criminal offence under the Health and Social Care Act 2008. New providers must submit a financial viability statement on CQC's own template.
- Sleep-in shifts and NMW: following Royal Mencap Society v Tomlinson-Blake [2021] UKSC 8, only time actually awake for the purposes of working counts for NMW during a sleep-in shift.
- Inter-call travel time and NMW: domiciliary care workers travelling between client homes are working for NMW purposes and must be paid at or above the applicable rate.
